The break-even computes on entered assumptions and FAILS -- it needs 790 stops a year against an entered capacity of 480 -- but those assumptions are fixtures and the real finding is which lever the arithmetic is sensitive to: order value and margin dominate the route cost at every stop count, so the thing to measure first is what a buyer orders, not what the driving costs.

the_position: Two investigations, eight operating models, six determinations. NOT ONE of the eight conclusions is SUPPORTED. The concrete investigation found that the capability it proposed to create already exists in the county, in a file Dula had on disk and had never read below the sector line; its economic relevance is CHALLENGED. The distribution investigation computes a break-even and the break-even fails, but on entered assumptions -- what the arithmetic actually establishes is that order value and margin dominate route cost, so the next measurement is a buyer's order and not a truck's mileage. In both cases the strongest-evidenced development strategy is somebody who already operates here doing slightly more, and in both cases forming a new company ranks last.
